title: PlanCommitted
description:
A conflict-free CollectionPlan has been committed atomically for one satellite over one horizon bucket. This event is published from the transactional outbox in the SAME transaction that inserted the acquisitions, so the event exists if and only if the plan exists — there is no window in which a consumer can see a plan that was rolled back, or miss one that was not.

What 'conflict-free' means, precisely, and what guarantees it:
  1. No two acquisitions on this satellite overlap. Guaranteed by a tstzrange + GiST EXCLUDE constraint in Postgres, not by application logic — so no future code path, migration, or manual INSERT can violate it.
  2. Consecutive acquisitions are separated by at least slew_time(a, b). Enforced by the planner and asserted by property-based tests over generated inputs.
  3. Per-orbit duty-cycle budget is respected.
  4. Every acquisition finishes before its request's deadline.

SUPERSESSION: a bucket can be planned more than once, because rounds fire on either a cadence timer or an opportunity debounce. plan_version increments per (satellite_id, bucket_start) and supersedes_plan_id points at the plan replaced. Consumers must treat a lower plan_version arriving after a higher one as stale and drop it — ordering is not assumed anywhere in this system.

causation_id.description: The event_id of the planning.round.triggered.v1 that opened this round.

plan_version.description: Monotonic per (satellite_id, bucket.start). Backed by an optimistic-concurrency version column on collection_plans: a concurrent commit at the same version loses and retries, rather than silently overwriting.

acquisitions.description: Ordered by window.start. An empty array is valid and meaningful: the satellite is deliberately idle for this bucket.

window.description: The committed acquisition interval — a concrete start chosen inside the opportunity's access_window, plus the dwell. This is the exact interval stored in the tstzrange column that the exclusion constraint guards.

slew_time_from_previous_s.description: Attitude manoeuvre plus settling time required after the preceding acquisition in this plan. Null-equivalent (absent) for the first acquisition. Carried on the event so the frontend timeline can render the slew gap as a real, occupied block rather than as apparent idle time — making the sequence-dependent setup cost visible is the difference between a Gantt chart and an explanation.

gap_from_previous_s.description: Actual idle time between the previous acquisition's end and this one's start. Must be >= slew_time_from_previous_s; the property-based test asserts this over arbitrary generated plans.

awarded_value_credits.description: Effective value this acquisition contributed to the objective: a function of bid, priority-tier multiplier, and ageing. The function itself is planner configuration, deliberately not part of the contract.

clearing_price_credits.description: What the winner would actually pay. Set only under VICKREY_SEALED_BID, where the winner pays the runner-up's bid — the second-price rule that makes truthful bidding the dominant strategy. Null under the greedy and exact policies, which are pure optimisers with no pricing rule attached.

metrics.description: The round's own scorecard. Carried on the event rather than only scraped from Prometheus so that policy comparison can be done by replaying the event log — the benchmark harness needs plan value and runtime side by side, per policy, over identical inputs.

satellite_utilisation_ratio.description: Imaging seconds committed divided by imaging seconds available in the bucket. Read alongside duty_cycle_used_s: high utilisation with an exhausted duty cycle means the constraint that bound was power, not time.

optimality_ratio.description: This plan's value divided by the EXACT_DP optimum for the same input. Populated only in the benchmark harness, where ExactDP is run as ground truth on instances small enough to solve. The whole point of the Strategy pattern is to make this number measurable rather than assumed.
